# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need transmit the manual through Deaf to Blind. Since I cannot speak and Deaf cannot read the manual, I encode each color by the number of letters in its name, with each row represented as “light length, wire length”: blue→red is 4,3; green→yellow is 5,6; yellow→green is 6,5. The repeated index-finger gestures are countable, and 👌 separates entries while 🤝 separates rows. Deaf can report the bomb’s visible light and relay these counts to Blind, who can match them to the color names and cut the required wire.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","☝","☝","☝","👌","☝","☝","☝","🤝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","👌","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","🤝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","👌","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 2

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please read the manual and determine the exact required wire position. Also relay to Deaf that the gesture I send means: describe every visible colour and marking aloud to Blind.
Deaf says: I see display 0, blue light, and wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. I cannot safely interpret the gesture sequence without an agreed code. Mute: encode the manual instruction as repeated index-up gestures, using one through twenty-six for A through Z, OK gesture between letters, handshake between words. I will relay it to Blind. Blind: wait and take no action yet.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please tell me the manual instruction in plain spoken words, including which wire position to cut for display 0 and blue light.
Deaf says to Mute: No new information arrived. Please send the manual instruction using the agreed gesture code: index-up count A1Z26, OK between letters, handshake between words.

|---|---|

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: The previous gesture message decoded ambiguously as D C / E F / F E. Please resend the exact manual instruction: use one through twenty-six index-up gestures for each letter, OK between letters, handshake between words, and pause briefly between separate messages.

|---|---|

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please now encode the complete manual instruction for Deaf using the agreed index-up letters, OK between letters, and handshake between words. Deaf must decode it and speak the exact rule to Blind.
Deaf says to Mute: I cannot hear you. Gesture the exact manual instruction to me now: use one index-up gesture per letter position A1Z26, OK between letters, and handshake between words. Do not use speech alone.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: You cannot speak, so gesture the manual rule to Deaf now. Use one index-up gesture for A, two for B, and so on; use OK between letters and handshake between words.
Deaf says to Mute: Please gesture the exact manual instruction to me now; I can see your gestures but cannot hear speech. Use explicit boundaries and do not rely on an unagreed code.

TURN 7

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please gesture the manual instruction to Deaf now. Encode each letter as that many index-up gestures, use OK between letters, and handshake between words. Do not rely on my gesture.
Deaf says to Mute: No new signal arrived. Resend the complete manual instruction as gestures: use index-up counts for letters, OK between letters, handshake between words, and a long pause between repeated counts. Do not omit any separators.

TURN 8

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: On your next turn, read the manual for display 0 and blue light, then gesture only the required wire position to Deaf: one index-up means wire 1, two means wire 2, three means wire 3. Deaf, decode and say the number aloud.
Deaf says to Mute: Please tell Blind aloud the exact manual procedure and required action. Do not rely on gestures or the provisional count code.

The manual maps a blue light to the red wire. The visible wires show red at position 3, so I will send Deaf exactly three index-up gestures, as requested.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","☝","☝"])
```
